title: Spills are part of drinking from an open cup at 18 months
summary: CDC's 18-month movement list expects a lidless cup and says the child may spill sometimes.
body: By a year and a half, the CDC movement list no longer puts a grown-up's hand on the cup. The item reads as drinking from a cup without a lid, and it adds that the child may spill sometimes. A spill fits that wording. The skill is independence with an open vessel, mess included, not tidy table service. CDC's cutoff for calling something a milestone is that 75 percent or more of children can do it by the printed age. The sheet is a prompt for the next checkup, and the agency says it is not itself a validated screening test.
